stops.name: Bradbury Landing
stops.fact: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater in August 2012 to investigate whether ancient environments could have supported microbial life.
stops.alt: Distant layered foothills of Mount Sharp beyond dark dunes, viewed from Curiosity’s landing site
stops.caption: 8–9 August 2012 · View from Bradbury Landing toward lower Mount Sharp. NASA’s cropped Mastcam mosaic, white-balanced to Earth-like lighting; original 2 km scale retained.
stops.observe: Look beyond the dark dunes to Mount Sharp’s distant layers. The 2 km scale shows how far this landscape extends.

stops.name: Yellowknife Bay
stops.fact: The early journey turned toward Yellowknife Bay. Later drilling there revealed evidence of an ancient freshwater lake and conditions favorable for microbial life.
stops.alt: Flat fractured rock and scattered stones at Yellowknife Bay
stops.caption: Sol 125 · Navcam at rover reference 5 / 1398. Monochrome panorama. Cropped detail.
stops.observe: Look at the flat rock broken into slabs by dark cracks.

stops.name: Across the plains
stops.fact: After its early investigations, Curiosity crossed the plains toward the layered foothills of Mount Sharp.
stops.alt: Open rocky plain with the low Cooperstown outcrop below the distant crater horizon
stops.caption: Sol 437 · 28 October 2013 · Rocky plains approaching Cooperstown. Monochrome, two-frame Navcam view. Earlier regional reference for this sol-504 stop.
stops.observe: Compare the scattered rocks and shallow outcrop with the open plain. This earlier view shows the same traverse region, rather than this stop’s exact viewpoint.

stops.name: Mount Sharp foothills
stops.fact: The mountain’s sedimentary layers let scientists compare environments preserved at different heights.
stops.caption: Sol 997 · Navcam at rover reference 48 / 1570. Monochrome panorama. Cropped detail.
stops.observe: Look at the large broken slabs scattered across the slope.

stops.name: Murray Buttes
stops.fact: Eroded buttes and layered sandstone record ancient sediment deposition. This is a regional stop, not the location of every named butte.
stops.alt: Angular layered outcrops above loose sandy talus at Murray Buttes
stops.caption: Sol 1454 · Murray Buttes. Mastcam regional reference from an earlier viewpoint than the sol-1500 stop.
stops.observe: Follow the broken ledges above the sandy slopes.

stops.name: Lower-mountain traverse
stops.fact: Curiosity continued investigating the lower mountain, comparing rocks along its ascent.
stops.alt: Low ridge, fractured rock and distant mountain slopes
stops.caption: Sols 1999–2000 · Navcam at rover reference 68 / 2626. Monochrome panorama. Cropped detail.
stops.observe: Look at the pale fractured rock exposed through darker soil.

stops.name: Glen Torridon · clay country
stops.fact: Glen Torridon’s clay-bearing rocks preserve evidence of interaction with water. Curiosity investigated this region from 2019 into 2021.
stops.caption: Sol 2481 · Mastcam view at Glen Etive. Raw camera color.
stops.observe: Compare the interpreted rock forms with the mission photograph.

stops.name: Leaving clay country
stops.fact: The tour leaves the Glen Torridon chapter and follows the higher traverse toward different mineral-bearing layers.
stops.alt: Layered Mont Mercou cliff with fractures and ledges visible in daylight
stops.caption: Sol 3074 · Mont Mercou in daylight, near the sol-3072 stop. Left Navcam.
stops.observe: Look at the cliff’s thin beds and larger vertical fractures.

stops.name: Toward sulfate-bearing slopes
stops.fact: Comparing clay-bearing and sulfate-bearing rocks helps scientists investigate changing water environments.
stops.alt: Sandy pockets and broken rock on sulfate-bearing slopes
stops.caption: Sol 3506 · Navcam at rover reference 95 / 3020. Monochrome panorama. Cropped detail.
stops.observe: Look at the eroded ridgeline and the broken rock below it.

stops.name: Gediz Vallis
stops.fact: Gediz Vallis Ridge preserves rocks transported by debris flows and later shaped by erosion.
stops.alt: Jumbled dark blocks on the low crest and apron of Gediz Vallis Ridge
stops.caption: 19 August 2023 · Gediz Vallis Ridge. Cropped Mastcam panorama; Earth-like color balance. Regional reference from an earlier viewpoint than the sol-3972 stop.
stops.observe: Compare the loose dark blocks with the finer material between them.

stops.name: Higher recorded traverse
stops.fact: Continue following the pinned rover journey up the mountain. This stop marks a historical position, rather than an invented future destination.
stops.alt: Small ridgeline on the right and Texoli butte on the left
stops.caption: Sol 4500 · Devil’s Gate ridge and the base of Texoli butte. Monochrome Navcam.
stops.observe: Look for the layered slope on the left and the broken ridge on the right.

stops.name: Recorded mountain frontier
stops.fact: This is the last rover position in this game’s recorded journey. Curiosity’s investigations continue to reveal how water shaped Mount Sharp.
stops.alt: Small disc-shaped mineral features in brushed bedrock
stops.caption: Sol 5016 · Salar de Vacas bedrock close-up, near the sol-5021 endpoint. MAHLI focus merge.
stops.observe: Photo: disc-shaped features just 3–4 mm across. Zoom in to inspect them.
